columnHelp.language: The course, by the language it teaches
columnHelp.status: Live: every part is in the app. Live, Incomplete: in the app, with more parts still to come. In Progress: being built, not in the app yet.
columnHelp.parts: The CEFR level the course teaches, then its parts in the app out of the parts it will have. A part is a stretch of the tree, such as First Steps
columnHelp.circles: Places on the course tree: lesson circles, help circles, Brush-Ups and Pick Your Own
columnHelp.words: Words in the course word list
columnHelp.tatoeba: Sentences taken from Tatoeba, a free collection of sentences translated by volunteers. Already written by speakers of the language
columnHelp.drafted: Sentences written for Tamago where Tatoeba had no good one
columnHelp.awaiting: Drafted sentences already used in lessons but not yet checked by a native speaker. It matches Drafted today because no checks have come back yet
columnHelp.coverage: How much of the official word list for the course's level (shown under Parts) the course teaches, with the list it is measured against under each number
columnHelp.lastDeploy: The newest version that changed this course
columnHelp.wiktionary: Words whose meaning and hint come from Wiktionary, the free dictionary, out of the course's words
columnHelp.linguaLibre: Words and sentences with a recording of a real person from Lingua Libre, a free library of recorded speech. Everything else is spoken by the device's own voice

levels.name: Part
levels.definition: A stage of A1, built around a theme.

levels.name: Circle
levels.definition: One topic node on the tree, pairing words with a grammar point.

levels.name: Round
levels.definition: Not a step you tap. Each circle is practiced 5 times over, with less help each pass: Round 1 recognizes, Round 5 recalls from scratch. You see it as the ring filling around the circle.

levels.name: Lesson
levels.definition: Not a step you tap. One ~10-question block, a single sitting; a round is split into lessons.

usage.tableDescription: The last 7 days. Most tokens are the earlier conversation, re-read from the cache on each reply.
